MCD.rationale: MCD's franchise model remains structurally excellent: ~95% franchised, ~90% gross margins, $13.9B franchise profit on $16.5B franchise revenue in 2025, and $38B TTM loyalty systemwide sales. Q1 2026 showed solid YoY growth (revenue +9.4%, EPS +6.9%) and operating cash flow of $2.41B. However, the near-term picture is clouded: CEO acknowledged consumer sentiment 'may be getting a little bit worse,' April comps were 'slightly negative,' Q2 comparable sales expected to 'decelerate meaningfully,' and restructuring charges plus a rising tax rate (22% vs 19.8%) create headwinds. The stock at $273.46 is just 3.6% above its 52-week low and ~20% below its high, with a forward P/E of ~20.3x representing a ~12% discount to the restaurant industry. This is mildly attractive — a quality franchise at a discount navigating a cyclical trough — but the deteriorating consumer environment, undefined NEXT strategy, and inability to verify valuation from the quant data pack limit conviction. The September investor day could serve as a catalyst if NEXT strategy details and traffic stabilization emerge.
